ISR.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3, line "SC-10 and SC-03": as worded, the effective writer count is 12 to 22 for every design under Zipf 0.99, below F_w = 64 (the proposed value; E-18, simulated), because nothing splits the hottest partition. Restated it still fails: P `fixN` fixes the partition count at define, which is the count SC-03 says nobody chooses (E-17: fails by definition), and filling by hash alone gives max/mean 1.58 at 16 groups even with the app split (E-18 B2).

V4.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3, line "SC-10 and SC-03": as worded, the effective writer count is 12 to 22 for every design under Zipf 0.99, below F_w = 64 (the proposed value; E-18, simulated), because nothing splits the hottest partition. Restated it still fails: v4 places rows on members by ring hash alone, with no move that follows load, and E-18 shows hash-only placement passes max/mean 1.25 before 16 groups even with the app split (reasoned from E-18's fixN runs; the ring itself was not run). With `replicas` unset every member holds every row, so writes do not grow with servers at all.

BUY.why: Step 1: on JetStream a resource is one stream (E-44). Step 2: a stream is one Raft group with one leader, so every write of the resource goes through one writer. Step 3: more servers add no writer, and spreading a resource over several streams is a count chosen by hand, so it fails as worded and restated (1.3 line "SC-10 and SC-03"): 1 writer against 64.

default.why: The slot move that grows a resource also empties a group (E-17: `shrink` holds, model-checked, crash-only), and the one-move policy has a margin against flapping (E-18: without it two pieces swapped for ever in 48 of 300 cases). But the 7-day cycle was not simulated, and nothing ran the rule that decides when to add or drop a group.
default.closes: Phase 2 sim: a daily load cycle over 7 days with the rule that adds and drops groups, counting grows and shrinks a day.

DRAFT.why: The same move empties a group (E-17, model-checked). But DRAFT's grow-and-shrink rule, run by each leader alone, was never simulated beyond the halving that does not balance (A-18), and no 7-day cycle ran.
DRAFT.closes: Phase 2 sim: a daily load cycle over 7 days with the rule that adds and drops groups, counting grows and shrinks a day. The rule must be the one each leader runs.

CELL.why: A re-key can go down as well as up (E-17: `shrink` holds in the model; "never shrinks" is a choice, not a rule limit). Each re-key copies the whole resource, which SC-08 judges. The 7-day cycle was not simulated.
CELL.closes: Phase 2 sim: a daily load cycle over 7 days with the rule that adds and drops groups, counting grows and shrinks a day.

LANE.why: Step 1: G `lane` fixes 64 groups per project and every resource hashes into them. Step 2: no option LANE holds adds or removes a lane. Step 3: so the group count cannot follow load: a project pays 64 groups whatever its load (E-17b, reasoned), and the test's "the group count follows load" cannot hold.

SPLIT.why: Step 1: P `split` splits a group by size and load and has no merge; merge is PD's option. Step 2: in E-17b's model a resource shrinks only through the merge protocol: "a split alone never shrinks". Step 3: so groups made at a peak stay for good, which is a lasting cost from a past peak.

ISR.why: Step 1: P `fixN` fixes N partitions per resource at define (Kafka's shape). Step 2: nothing removes or merges a partition, and N has to be sized for the peak. Step 3: so the group count stays at its peak size when load falls (E-17: fixN fails SC-04).

PD.why: Split + merge shrinks in the model (E-17b: `shrink` holds with the merge, 11 more rules), and TiKV merges regions in production (cited). The 7-day cycle was not simulated here.
PD.closes: Phase 2 sim: a daily load cycle over 7 days with the rule that adds and drops groups, counting grows and shrinks a day.

V4.why: v4 has no groups to grow. Members leave by ballot, and a scoped leave hands its partitions on first (V4-6, V4-38), so replicas shrink back. No daily cycle was run on it.
V4.closes: A 7-day load cycle in v4's sim, with members joining and leaving.

BUY.why: One stream per resource: nothing grows, so nothing has to shrink back, and replica counts change only by an operator's command. No cycle was run.
BUY.closes: A 7-day cycle on a JetStream cluster (not planned: BUY is the reference row).

default.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3, line "SC-05 at 10 GB": one Node process wakes 10 GB of 2 KB rows in 86 to 122 s against 60 s (5 GB in 36 s). The time is v4's JS crc32c and decode, not the design, and A-13's faster wake (a native crc32c, a format V8 decodes whole, blind writes while the fold catches up) is planned and not built. Restated per storage form it is still open: no sleep and wake test ran against an S3-compatible store, with disks kept or lost.
default.closes: Build A-13's faster wake and re-run E-34 (G-29); with the object-store tier, the sleep and wake test with disks kept and with disks lost.

SRV.why: Its server folds plain rows natively, so E-34's Node figure (86 to 122 s) and the 1.3 line do not apply. A native wake of 10 GB was not measured (E-34 reasons it is faster), and no sleep and wake test ran against a store.
SRV.closes: Measure a native wake of 10 GB; the sleep and wake test with disks kept and lost.

PD.why: Step 1: PD keeps its log and state in S `lsm` on each server's own disk, with no `+tier` and no log tier (SPACE 4.1). Step 2: SC-05's test stops every server and wakes with servers that lost their disks. Step 3: then no copy is left anywhere, so acknowledged writes are lost.

V4.why: Step 1: v4 keeps a WAL per resource on each server's own disk (S `walg`), with no object-store tier and no log tier (SPACE 4.1). Step 2: SC-05's test stops every server and wakes with servers that lost their disks. Step 3: then no copy is left anywhere, so acknowledged writes are lost; with disks kept v4 does wake (J: 1.4 s for 312 rows).

BUY.why: Step 1: JetStream keeps a stream on its servers' file store (E-44) and has no object-store tier. Step 2: SC-05's test stops every server and wakes with servers that lost their disks. Step 3: then the streams are gone, so acknowledged writes are lost.

default.why: By design only: cold rows are read through from snapshot layers on disk or in the object store, opt in per resource, and groups spread over servers (DESIGN-V5 4.1, marked "later"). No experiment ran a data set at 3 × RAM, and a cold row cannot be a sync read (X15).

PD.why: S `lsm` holds state larger than memory by construction (SPACE section 2, S), as TiKV and CockroachDB do in production, and regions spread over servers. A cold read is a local disk read, under one object-store get (about 30 ms on S3, cited in E-28). Not measured here.

V4.why: v4 keeps every row a server holds in memory and has no cold rows and no object-store tier. `replicas: N` spreads partitions over members, which covers the disk half only.

BUY.why: E-44's client folds the whole stream into memory, and one stream sits whole on each of its replicas, so a resource cannot pass one server's disk without a hand-chosen number of streams.

default.why: The idle cost at n = 100 is stated: 0.95% of a core in Node and 0.33% in Rust for 99 pinged links and 2,000 quiet groups, 19,800 frames a second in all (E-25). The knob past 100 is A-12's bound on linked peers per member. But no v5 kernel ran a sim sweep at n = 100.
default.closes: Phase 2: the sim's n = 100 sweep, as v4's scale tier, with the idle cost and A-12's peer bound pinned.

V4.why: v4's sim runs its n = 100 scale tier in `npm test` (the test SC-07 names), and DESIGN-SCALE states the idle frames per tick at n = 100 and a design range of 1 to 100 members.

ISR.why: Its idle follower fetches are pairwise: about 34,000 to 40,000 frames a second at n = 100 above 1e4 partitions (E-25, counted from cited Kafka defaults). No sim ran at n = 100.
ISR.closes: Phase 2: the sim's n = 100 sweep, as v4's scale tier, with the idle cost and A-12's peer bound pinned.

SLOG.why: Servers keep one session each to the controller: 400 idle frames a second at n = 100 and no peer bound needed (E-25, counted). No sim ran at n = 100.
SLOG.closes: Phase 2: the sim's n = 100 sweep, as v4's scale tier, with the idle cost and A-12's peer bound pinned.

OBJ.why: It sends no idle frames, but a lease renewed by PUT costs 500 to 50,000 PUTs a second at n = 100 unless leases go quiet (E-25, counted). No sim ran at n = 100.
OBJ.closes: Phase 2: the sim's n = 100 sweep, as v4's scale tier, with the idle cost and A-12's peer bound pinned.

PD.why: TiKV runs past 100 stores in production with store heartbeats to its controller (cited). No sim of this shape ran here at n = 100, and its idle cost was not stated.
PD.closes: Phase 2: the sim's n = 100 sweep, as v4's scale tier, with the idle cost and A-12's peer bound pinned.

BUY.why: The sim cannot run nats-server's bytes (TEST-10), so only a real run of 100 servers could show this, and none was made.
BUY.closes: A real 100-server JetStream run (not planned: BUY is the reference row).

default.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3, line "SC-08(b)": a three-commit slot move is unwritable 16.7 ms at p99 under 10,000 writes a second against 10 ms and a one-commit move stays at or under 4.7 ms (E-13); A-17 cuts the move to one or two commits, but that cut was never model-checked with unclean recovery (K-03). The move is safe and copies only its own slot in the models (E-15, E-17c) and a new group takes its 1/G share (E-18), but no sweep ran moves with membership changes (K-01) and (c) was never pinned. Restated to a p50 plus a load-tied p99 it is open for the same reasons.
default.closes: Before phase 1: model the cut move with unclean recovery (K-03) and a sweep of moves with membership changes (K-01, K-02). Phase 2: pins for (b), (c) and (f) with the real carried set (K-25).

CELL.why: E-17c's model of the re-key fails on every bound. A write to a partition that never moves waits for the re-key's cut-over (L8: SC-08(b), "while others go on"), and that partition's rows are copied to the new generation (F8: SC-08(f)).

LANE.why: Lanes never move in v5, so a scale change is a replica change only, and that is model-checked one group at a time (A-01, A-19). No sweep with scale events ran, and (c) and (f) were not pinned.
LANE.closes: Phase 2: the sim sweep with servers added and removed, and pins for (c) and (f).

SPLIT.why: A split touches only what it moves and copies no rows (E-17c: L8 and F8 hold, crash-only). Its unwritable window was not timed, and no sweep ran splits with membership changes.
SPLIT.closes: Time the split's window as E-13 did for the slot move; phase 2: the sim sweep and pins.

PD.why: Split + merge holds L8 and F8 in the model (E-17c), but a merge freezes every partition of the group it removes (E-17b, reasoned), and that window was not timed here.
PD.closes: Time the merge's freeze as E-13 did for the slot move; a sweep with scale events.

ISR.why: Its partitions never move between groups, so a scale change is a replica reassignment by its controller. No model or sweep of that ran here, and (c) and (f) were not pinned.
ISR.closes: A sim sweep of replica reassignments under its controller, with pins for (c) and (f).

V4.why: v4's sim sweeps joins and leaves with monitors, but STATUS lists open cases: a held member that needs an operator, and a drain at one replica that loses rows when the new holder crashes. (b), (c) and (f) are not pinned at these bars.
V4.closes: Close STATUS's open membership cases, and pin (b), (c) and (f) in v4's scale tier.

BUY.why: The sim cannot run nats-server (TEST-10), and JetStream moves a stream's replicas only when an operator asks (cited from memory, not checked here). No scale event was run in E-44.
BUY.closes: A real-cluster run that adds and removes JetStream servers under load.

Restated to a p50 plus a load-tied p99 it is still open: no sweep ran.
OBJ.closes: Before phase 1: model the cut move with unclean recovery (K-03) and a sweep of moves with membership changes (K-01, K-02). Phase 2: pins for (b), (c) and (f) with the real carried set (K-25).

default.why: One Node server held 10,000 idle links in 89 MB at 0.88% of a core, and 1,000 active subscribers at 10 messages a second cost 8.8% of a core (17% over TLS) with p99 2.0 ms (E-27). That is both counts on under a fifth of a core. A-11 puts a TLS terminator in front, because 10,000 TLS links take 538 MB in Node.

SRV.why: Its edge is native. E-08's Rust relay served 1,000 and 10,000 subscriber sockets from one core (13.4 and 11.9 million deliveries a second), so both counts hold. Idle-link memory in a native TLS stack was not measured (reasoned to be under Node's).

EMB-V8.why: Its edge is native. E-08's Rust relay served 1,000 and 10,000 subscriber sockets from one core (13.4 and 11.9 million deliveries a second), so both counts hold. Idle-link memory in a native TLS stack was not measured (reasoned to be under Node's).

V4.why: J shows 1,240 browser links on one v4 project. 10,000 idle links were not measured on v4's own kernel, which answers every link's heartbeat on the one event loop that also folds and runs user code (M `loop`).

BUY.why: Clients link to nats-server. E-09b measured its fan-out to 16 subscribers (4.13 million deliveries a second), not 10,000 idle links or 1,000 subscribers on a core.

default.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3, line "SC-13's small": per-slot state costs about 85 B per touched slot in Node (E-36). With a run-length slot table, sparse per-slot state and dormant groups (A-15, A-16) an idle resource costs 1.4 KB at 10 touched slots and 8.8 KB at 100, against 2 KB; a create takes 4.6 to 5.3 ms against 10.7 ms, and a cold open 3.3 to 3.5 ms at the median but 5.4 to 7.6 ms at worst against 5 ms. As worded "small" is undefined; restated as "few slots touched" the memory clause holds, and it stays open because 1e5 resources (the proposed N_res) were not created and dropped through `fero()` and the drop clauses were not run.
default.closes: Phase 2: the sim that creates and drops 1e5 resources at 100 a second through `fero()`, with a cold-open pin (G-16) and the drop clauses.

MIN-P.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3, line "SC-13's small": per-slot state costs about 85 B per touched slot in Node (E-36). With G `pslot` an idle resource costs 0.4 to 1.2 KB at 1 to 10 touched slots in about 16 project groups, with no dormant groups, and a create takes 1.6 to 1.8 ms against 10.7 ms; at 100 touched slots it passes 2 KB either way. As worded "small" is undefined; restated as "few slots touched" the memory clause holds, and it stays open because a resource dropped out of a shared group was never run (K-06) and 1e5 resources (the proposed N_res) were not created through `fero()`.
MIN-P.closes: Phase 2: the sim that creates and drops 1e5 resources at 100 a second through `fero()`, with a cold-open pin (G-16) and the drop clauses. Also K-06: a drop out of a shared group.

SLOG.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3, line "SC-13's small": per-slot state costs about 85 B per touched slot in Node (E-36). SLOG takes A-15 by reasoning only: E-26 counts one group per resource for it, and a loglet's idle cost was not measured. So it is open as worded and restated, at the proposed N_res of 100,000.
SLOG.closes: Measure a dormant loglet's idle cost; then Phase 2: the sim that creates and drops 1e5 resources at 100 a second through `fero()`, with a cold-open pin (G-16) and the drop clauses.

OBJ.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3, line "SC-13's small": per-slot state costs about 85 B per touched slot in Node (E-36). OBJ holds no group in memory (E-26), so its idle cost is the catalog row, the slot table and the touched slots; a create is a manifest PUT. None of this was measured for OBJ, so it is open as worded and restated, at the proposed N_res of 100,000.
OBJ.closes: Price an idle resource and a create on OBJ; then Phase 2: the sim that creates and drops 1e5 resources at 100 a second through `fero()`, with a cold-open pin (G-16) and the drop clauses.

CELL.why: CELL has 16 groups per resource: 1.6 million groups for 1e5 resources, which fit only as dormant groups at 57 B each (A-15, E-26), about 0.9 KB a resource before its cell state. E-36 did not price CELL's create of 16 groups or its idle resource.

LANE.why: An idle resource costs 0.2 KB, a create takes 1.6 to 1.8 ms and the project keeps 64 groups whatever the resource count (E-36). Not run: the 1e5 create-and-drop sim, and a drop that frees one resource's space out of a lane's shared log.

ISR.closes: The phase with learners and relays: the sim with 80 to 150 ms links between regions (no false failover, Q-21's lease and TTL checks, far-read lag).

V4.closes: A v4 sim with 80 to 150 ms links, and a rule that keeps far members out of the view.

PD.why: TiKV runs learners and follower reads across regions (cited), and its time comes from one oracle (T `tso`), so a far write pays a trip to it. No sim ran here with far links.
PD.closes: The phase with learners and relays: the sim with 80 to 150 ms links between regions (no false failover, Q-21's lease and TTL checks, far-read lag).

OBJ.why: OBJ has no voters: the writer holds a lease by CAS on the store, so "home region" means the store's region. A far write then pays a PUT across regions; nothing measured or simulated it.
OBJ.closes: The phase with learners and relays: the sim with 80 to 150 ms links between regions (no false failover, Q-21's lease and TTL checks, far-read lag).

BUY.why: JetStream follows across regions through mirrors and leaf nodes (cited from memory, not checked here). The sim cannot run it, and no far-link run was made.
BUY.closes: A real JetStream run with 80 to 150 ms links.
